newsitem.title: USA: Salt may relieve chronic fatigue syndrome - study.
newsitem.headline: Salt may relieve chronic fatigue syndrome - study.

text.p: Increasing salt intake may relieve the symptoms of chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS), researchers reported on Tuesday at an American College of Cardiology conference.
Dr. Satyendra Giri, a clinical investigator at Hartford Hospital in Connecticut, recently led a study involving 37 diagnosed CFS sufferers.

Of the group, 31 revealed in interviews that they were on low-salt diets for no medical reason. Of those 31, tests showed 25 suffered from neurally mediated hypotension, a nervous system disorder related to CFS, Giri reported.
After testing, all 37 patients were put on higher salt and water diets. Giri reported that 51 percent of them said afterward that their CFS symptoms were at least partially relieved.
Restricting salt intake is harmless for most people, but for those predisposed to CFS for various reasons, limiting salt intake can aggravate the hypotension that is related to CFS, Giri said.
"There's a lot of scepticism about the disease. I started as a sceptic myself, but there are a lot of people really suffering from this disease," Giri said.
"CFS symptoms, which are so incapacitating, can be improved just by putting the patient on a high salt and water diet," he said.
